answers.answer: The `alerts/infra/` event-driven alert-delivery stack owns all three paths: QuickNode webhooks through the on-chain event Cloud Function to Slack, the Sentry-to-Slack bridge, and the Splunk On-Call announcer that posts to `#eng` and reconciles `@support-engineer`. It is separate from `alerts/rules/`, which owns Grafana metric rules and their notification routing. Treat any change as live multi-provider infrastructure: plan first, expect `pnpm alerts:infra:plan` to show zero changes except the intended delta, and review the CI plan. Never apply locally; apply only after merge to `main` through the `production-infra` required-reviewer gate, with explicit human approval. Do not partially override the `multisigs` map because that can silently stop monitoring omitted Safes. Preserve the QuickNode state-management module name, and run `bash alerts/infra/scripts/fix-webhook-state.test.sh` when changing its parser, repair tool, or replacement provisioner. For handler or announcer code changes, keep the standalone lockfile in sync and require typecheck, coverage, lint, and knip to pass; run the path-aware quality gate for combined edits.

evidence.supports: Defines the two independent Terraform stacks and assigns QuickNode delivery, Sentry-to-Slack, and on-call announcements to `alerts/infra/`.

Requires explicit approval before apply, warns that the stack talks to live external APIs, documents the QuickNode state-management naming hazard and standalone lockfiles, and confirms the active Slack delivery paths.
Lists stack plan, component test, QuickNode state repair test, combined quality-gate, and deploy-verification checks.
Warns against partial multisig overrides and requires initialization, planning, CI plan review, and production-infra-gated apply after merge rather than local apply.
Requires reviewing webhook replacements and routes applies and destroys through the production-infra gate, with explicit human approval for destroys.
